content: The Tribunal of Brescia evaluated a claim to deviate from the 50/50 ownership presumption in a marital home. The plaintiff argued that 8/10 of the property was a personal asset funded by an "indirect donation" from his father. The court strictly applied Article 179 of the Civil Code, requiring proof of a specific link between the gift and the purchase. It ruled that generic bank transfers from a parent do not automatically qualify the resulting purchase as personal. Without documented proof of an animus donandi specifically targeting that real estate, the presumption of joint ownership prevails. Legal statements made during the separation process were deemed too vague to create a binding obligation for higher shares. Consequently, the judge declared the parties equal co-owners of the apartment. The property was found indivisible and subsequently referred to the evidentiary stage for sale operations.
